A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Batched NSGDM study, including Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–D. The algorithm, equations, theorem statements and proofs are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical bounds, proofs and an analytical example, including in its appendices. Empirical observations are attributed to other work; no original experiments or data analyses are reported.

after.justification: v4 retains the theoretical study without adding original empirical results. Its new concurrent-work citations also do not constitute experiments produced by this paper.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same gradient averaging, momentum update and normalized step. Its parameter prescriptions and the sign-based variant in Remark 3.1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Appendix A retains the same analytical example, rather than introducing an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The analytical comparison with Clipped SGD in Section 4 is retained. The newly cited concurrent methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The theoretical batch sizes, stepsizes and momentum choices in the main and appendix theorems remain unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablations or robustness experiments are added or removed. The analytical example and supplementary discussions in Appendices A–C are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The probabilistic bounds are theoretical results, not empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Theorems 3.2, 3.3 and 3.6 retain the same convergence and lower-complexity bounds, as do their appendix counterparts. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The assumptions, lemmas, theorem statements and derivations remain unchanged, including the generalized-smoothness equivalence, martingale inequality and upper/lower-bound proofs in Appendices A–D. The new lower-bound citation supplies no new proof or formal result of this work.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a footnote qualifying its priority claim by acknowledging two independent concurrent works with similar results. The claimed convergence rates and scope under generalized assumptions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The normalization explanation, restrictions involving L1 and sigma1, loss of noise-level adaptivity, and general unknown-p minimax question remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode and theoretical parameter prescriptions are retained. Neither version supplies experimental implementation settings, and no code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: v4 adds the heavy-tailed normalization papers by Hübler, Fatkhullin and He (2024) and Sun, Liu and Yuan (2024). Section 1.1 acknowledges their concurrent results and credits Hübler and colleagues with a matching lower bound for Batched NSGD with zero momentum.

P1.justification: Limited edits add contribution footnotes and rewrite the Section 2 problem statement to explicitly emphasize minimizing the gradient norm, already described in v2's introduction. Section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the page 2 footnote block, places Section 2's minimization expression inline, and reflows references so long URLs no longer extend beyond the page edge. Algorithm 1 remains in place; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v4 improves attribution by acknowledging concurrent results and a related matching lower bound omitted from v2. It also clarifies the objective and fixes overflowing reference URLs. The scientific results and proofs are unchanged, and Section 3.1 still retains 'first and only' wording, so the attribution correction remains incomplete.
